comparison: Perfect agreement on centrosome size scaling with cell size (C46-C48). Both evaluations find the model successfully reproduces experimental scaling behavior across organisms. OpenEval emphasizes analytical derivations and parameter analysis, while peer reviewers highlight enhanced comparison to experimental results in revision.

Perfect agreement on localized enzyme model (C57-C58). Both confirm that enzyme localization leads to robustness problems similar to autocatalytic models, demonstrating the importance of enzyme sharing. This serves as a control comparison in both evaluations.

Strong agreement on background claims (C1-C10). Both evaluations accept these as well-established foundational facts about centrosome structure, function, and cell cycle. OpenEval notes appropriate citations to prior literature; peer reviewers treat these as uncontroversial context.

Strong agreement on enzyme-dependent predictions (C71-C74). Both evaluations support these testable predictions. OpenEval emphasizes alignment with experimental observations; peer reviewers note the authors propose concrete experiments to test the theory and carefully discuss parameter values.

Strong agreement on autocatalytic model failure (C11-C14, C63-C64, C67). Both confirm the model demonstrates autocatalytic approaches cannot robustly control size equality. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical framework and simulations; peer reviewers describe this as 'compelling evidence' and note the paper is well-written.

Strong agreement on catalytic model success (C18, C36-C41, C60, C62). Both evaluations confirm the shared-enzyme catalytic model reproduces experimental observations and ensures size equality. OpenEval cites specific figures and quantitative fits; peer reviewers note 'compelling evidence' and enhanced experimental comparisons. Peer R2 also includes C44-C45, C75-C77 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Strong agreement on molecular mechanisms (C29-C33, C54-C56). Both evaluations accept the biological foundation for catalytic growth involving PCM accumulation catalyzed by centrioles and enzymes. OpenEval emphasizes citations to established experimental findings; peer reviewers accept this framework without objection.

Agreement on autocatalytic model limitations (C24-C25, C27-C28, C53). Both evaluations support the systematic exploration of model limitations through parameter space analysis. These claims overlap with peer R1's broader evaluation of autocatalytic model failure.

Agreement on diffusion timescale separation (C19-C20, C83). Both evaluations accept the justification for reaction-limited modeling. OpenEval cites theoretical calculations and FRAP data; peer reviewers explicitly note that Appendix 4 addresses finite diffusion concerns and significantly improved the manuscript.

Agreement on constant enzyme concentration results (C44-C45). OpenEval finds these claims supported by simulations showing shared catalysis is key. Peer R2 includes these claims in broader evaluation of catalytic model success, accepting the mechanism rather than enzyme limitation drives size equality.

Agreement on C. elegans growth curves (C42), though with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct quantitative measurements, relying on indirect PCM assembly dynamics. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, explicitly noting the model reproduces these growth curves as compelling evidence.

Agreement on enzyme sharing mechanism (C34, C68, C70). Both evaluations support the inference of shared enzyme pools from FRAP data and diffusion calculations. OpenEval acknowledges need for direct experimental validation; peer reviewers accept the molecular basis without objection.

Agreement on prior literature context (C5, C17). Both evaluations accept these citations to established views and prior work. OpenEval notes appropriate context for the study; peer reviewers explicitly state the work builds on these ideas without disputing the characterization.

Partial overlap on asymmetry and mechanistic details. OpenEval R9 addresses asymmetric predictions (C51, C77-C78); peer R13 addresses supporting mechanistic details (C51, C65-C66). Both support C51 on asymmetric centrosome sizes in Drosophila as testable predictions.

Agreement on testable predictions (C76). OpenEval emphasizes these predictions distinguish the catalytic model from alternatives. Peer R2 includes C76 in broader evaluation, with peer R8 explicitly noting the authors propose concrete experiments to test the theory.

Agreement on cooperativity requirement (C24). Both evaluations support that non-cooperative models fail. OpenEval includes this in parameter space analysis; peer R12 treats it as a negative control showing some cooperativity is needed.

Agreement on molecular interaction inference (C65). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting sound reasoning consistent with experimental findings though representing interpretation. Peer R13 accepts this as supporting mechanistic detail without challenge.

Agreement on Ostwald ripening distinction (C66). Both evaluations accept this citation to Zwicker et al. 2014. OpenEval notes it distinguishes growth-induced inequality from ripening effects; peer reviewers accept it as context for phase separation phenomena.

Partial overlap on parameter values and timescales (C80, C82). OpenEval addresses timescale separation justifying modeling approach; peer R11 notes authors carefully discuss parameter values without raising concerns about these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses limiting pool assumption (C35) supported by Decker et al. 2011 citation, acknowledging it may not apply universally. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer R6 accepts related molecular mechanisms without objection.
